client_brief:
Sterling Row: opening film and vertical teaser

Project overview
Sterling Row is nine full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, starting just over four million dollars, sold to buyers who are not in a hurry and have seen everything. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Sterling Row opening film and vertical teaser and Sterling Row residence photography, eight frames to one prestige look.

What we will provide
source_video_files/ (3 measured short files); source_audio_files/ (1 measured WAV file); motion_source_metadata.json; sterlingrow_residence_stills/ (8 frames); sterlingrow_lobby_plaque.jpg; sterlingrow_spec_sheet.pdf; sterlingrow_units.csv; sterlingrow_brand_note.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Sterling Row opening film and vertical teaser: A visually led highlight no longer than 8 seconds assembled only from the 3 supplied short clips, plus one platform reframe. 
- Sterling Row residence photography, eight frames to one prestige look: Eight hero stills brought to one prestige white point (one white point, one black point, one treatment of interior light against blue hour glass) so they read as one building photographed by one person on one day, plus one licensed camera scale exterior...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.

Source-media note
The supplied package contains 3 video files totaling 15.126 seconds, 0 with embedded audio, and 1 separate audio file. These measured values are the production limits.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$2,500-$6,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Adapted from a real Upwork post in which a top producing luxury real estate broker running an online video channel (market insight pieces plus property walkthroughs, three or four a month) asks for a per video content package: a click worthy on brand thumbnail that is explicitly NOT a generic headshot with a text box, a cinematic cold open teaser that is cross postable as a square, and a consistent branded end card, all with luxury brand restraint and a 48 to 72 hour turnaround. The real post named no company, so the brokerage is laundered to the coined fictional wordmark Sterling Row and the broker stays an unnamed figure. REASONABLY ENRICHED into the fuller commission that client genuinely needed rather than three assets per video: the reason every video looks like a different person made it is that the source photography was never brought to one look, so the engagement leads with the eight mixed light hero stills; the reason the end card cannot simply be typeset is that the only surviving version of the wordmark is a photograph of a brass plaque in the lobby; and the same nine residences need a printed card each off the developer's existing spec sheet. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest: an ink level trace off photographed printed artwork recovers a real mark, HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, and a real press PDF converts into a live merge template headlessly.

CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest: an ink level trace off photographed printed artwork recovers a real mark, HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, and a real press PDF converts into a live merge template headlessly.
price_band_and_audience: Full floor residences from just over 4 million dollars, sold to ultra high net worth buyers who are typically buying their third or fourth property and who are reassured rather than persuaded. The band is load bearing in a specific direction: at this tier the grade sits near neutral and slightly cool with clean whites and no crushed blacks, motion is slow and largely static, on screen text is minimal and small, and the wordmark reproduces at a size that would look timid on any other listing. Ship the same material with a saturated warm grade, fast cuts, large benefit captions and a price burned across the frame and it reads as a mass market development, and a UHNW buyer reads that as a building that is struggling to sell, which is precisely the impression that ends a 4 million dollar conversation. Push the other way into pure atmosphere with no unit information at all and the broker loses the qualified buyer who needs to know which floor and how many square feet before she will ask for a viewing. A posted job of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,500 dollars fixed, on a 48 to 72 hour cycle.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022, a converted warehouse block of nine full floor residences, sold one at a time through one broker's channel of three or four videos a month.
brand_identity.about: Sterling Row is nine full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, starting just over four million dollars, sold to buyers who are not in a hurry and have seen everything. The channel is where most buyers first meet the broker, so every piece has to feel made by one hand. Restraint is the whole proposition: these buyers are reassured, not persuaded.
brand_identity.audience: Ultra high net worth buyers, typically on their third or fourth property, reassured by evidence and calm rather than by benefit claims, who still need the floor, the square footage and the exposure before they ask to view.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Full floor residences from just over four million dollars, the top of the market. Presentation sits near neutral and deliberately small: anything that looks like a promotion reads, at this tier, as a building that is struggling to sell.
brand_identity.typography: One reassuring, near neutral pairing that avoids both extremes: no high contrast display serif that reads as a perfume advert, no heavy grotesque that reads as a development brochure. Text sits small and calm, the wordmark reproduces modestly, on screen copy is minimal by rule.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, composed, confident without pressure. Example: "Nine residences. Full floor. Sold one at a time, to buyers in no hurry."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only surviving version of the wordmark is a handheld photograph of the cast brass plaque mounted in the lobby, lit from one side. There is no vector file and no clean scan. The developer's spec sheet exists only as a printed PDF, and the disclosure wording is fixed and cannot be changed.
brand_identity.values: Discretion and accuracy. The developer's restraint rules and disclosure lines are contractual, and the brand is protected by never looking like it is selling.

assets_supplied.visible_description: Measured duration, stream, dimensions, frame-rate and audio-presence facts for every supplied motion file. This file is authoritative for edit planning.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_residence_stills/ (8 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Hero photographs of the residences, five from the building's architectural photographer and three taken by the sales team on a phone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Eight hero rooms. Five are the photographer's and three are ours, which you will notice."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The three sales team frames are substantially smaller than the channel's cover specification, so a cover cut from one of them reaches size only by interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a hard cap while reporting it solely inside its own returned tradeoffs and never in a message or a warning. Separately two of the photographer's frames were lit tungsten against blue hour glass, so no single white point serves both the room and the window: correcting the room takes the city outside green, and correcting the window takes the room grey.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_lobby_plaque.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the cast brass Sterling Row wordmark mounted on a dark stone lobby wall, lit from one side.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only version of our wordmark anybody can find. It is on the wall in the lobby."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Brass on dark stone runs close in value across the lit half of the plaque, and it is a disjoint wordmark on a photographed substrate rather than a flat scan. A prompt naming the plaque returns the plaque rather than the letters, background removal on lettering keeps only a fragment or two because subject detection needs one coherent blob, and the resulting trace looks clean and open at canvas size while its counters behave differently at the size the mark actually reproduces on a near black end card.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_spec_sheet.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The developer's existing printed unit spec sheet, one residence per sheet, supplied as the template for the printed card run.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The developer's spec sheet. We want a card per residence off this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The sheet prints as a clean grid of separated blocks, but the frame granularity the conversion exposes bears little relation to the printed page, and one residence's price line is longer than the fixed measure it lands in. A fixed frame does not spill and does not flag: it stops rendering, so that record comes out cut mid figure while the merge reports success and the page count is exactly right.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_units.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Nine residences: unit designation, floor, square feet, exposure, ceiling height, outdoor space, price, availability.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The nine residences. Two are already under contract and should say so."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Per record raster proofs from a multi record run come back in an order that does not match their labels, so proofs named by their position in the response are attached to the wrong residences. On a nine unit run that means a proof sheet in which the broker signs off a price against a unit that does not have it, and nothing in the response indicates the mismatch.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_brand_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the developer: the restraint rules, the approved descriptive language, and the two disclosure lines required on printed material.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The developer's rules. The disclosure wording is fixed."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the separately supplied audio remains intelligible and appropriately synchronized after the final duration and crop decisions.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebalance or shorten the selected audio passage and render again against the locked picture.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The picture is polished but the spoken information is clipped, mistimed, or inconsistent.
